chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man wants to perform istinja'; how should he sit? He said: "As he sits for defecation." And he said: "He is only required to wash what is outwardly visible of it, and he is not required to wash its interior."

key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: defecation; the act for which the sitting posture is being compared
key_terms.ظَهَرَ: what is outwardly visible or external
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinja', cleansing the private area after relieving oneself
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ: to wash as an act of purification
key_terms.يَقْعُدُ: to sit in the prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: How should a person sit for istinja', and is washing the interior required?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the manner of sitting for istinja' and the extent of washing required. It states that one sits as for relieving oneself and that only the outwardly visible area must be washed, not the interior.
